title: Who is backpacking for
paragraphs: Do you know anyone who has gone backpacking? It's a type of travel that is low-cost and independent, often meaning no fixed plans regarding accommodation or destination. The word 'backpacking' comes from 'backpack', a type of bag that you carry on your back. Travellers typically fill a backpack with life essentials, like clothing, plus anything extra needed for adventure. The stereotypical view of a backpacker is someone in their 20s, keen to tick off items on their bucket list.
But, forget this. You're about to find out that anyone can backpack.

Last year, my best friend's parents retired at aged 65 and set off on a 630-mile trail along the southwest coast of England. Each carrying a 15kg backpack, Mike and Lorraine hiked along cliffs, explored golden sandy beaches and even cycled. For accommodation, they didn't pre-book but stayed in whatever they could find on the day, which varied from B&Bs to camping in fields full of sheep. They did stop for the occasional well-deserved cup of tea – they were in England after all.

Backpackers are also known for travelling with little money, but few begin with as little as Othmane Zolati from Morocco. In 2015, he embarked on an almost four-year journey, but he started out with just $80 (£64). He zigzagged across 24 countries on the African continent and filmed his experience, aiming to show the world the diversity and beauty of Africa, all on a shoestring budget. He told BBC What's New that he often had to work odd jobs and rely on the kindness of strangers to be able to afford to keep travelling. But it was worth it. South Africa was Othmane's final destination and, on reaching it, he said "It was one of the best moments in my life. It made me know that if you fight for something, you really stick to that goal… then you will reach it".
So, don't give up. If you want to travel, you can, no matter your age or budget!

vocabulary.example: They went backpacking in Europe for two months.
vocabulary.translation: 他们去欧洲背包旅行了两个月。

vocabulary.example: The price includes flights and hotel accommodation.
vocabulary.translation: 这个价格包括机票和酒店住宿。

vocabulary.example: Thailand is a popular tourist destination.
vocabulary.translation: 泰国是一个受欢迎的旅游目的地。

vocabulary.example: He packed all his camping gear into his backpack.
vocabulary.translation: 他把所有露营装备都装进了背包。

vocabulary.entry: **essential** /ɪˈsenʃl/ n. 必需品；不可或缺的东西
vocabulary.example: I only had time to pack the bare essentials.
vocabulary.translation: 我只有时间打包最基本的必需品。

vocabulary.entry: **stereotypical** /ˌsteriəˈtɪpɪkl/ adj. 刻板印象的；模式化的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film is full of stereotypical characters.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影里充斥着刻板印象的人物。

vocabulary.example: She was keen to get started on the project.
vocabulary.translation: 她渴望开始这个项目。

vocabulary.entry: **tick off** /ˌtɪk ˈɒf/ phr. v. 打勾标记；快速列出（口语）
vocabulary.example: I managed to tick off a few more things on my to-do list.
vocabulary.translation: 我设法在待办事项清单上又勾掉了几件事。

vocabulary.entry: **bucket list** /ˈbʌkɪt lɪst/ n. 人生愿望清单；遗愿清单（口语）
vocabulary.example: Skydiving is at the top of my bucket list.
vocabulary.translation: 跳伞是我人生愿望清单上的首要事项。

vocabulary.example: My father retired from teaching last year.
vocabulary.translation: 我父亲去年从教学岗位退休了。

vocabulary.entry: **set off** /ˌset ˈɒf/ phr. v. 出发；动身
vocabulary.example: We set off early the next morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我们第二天一早出发了。

vocabulary.example: We followed a winding trail through the forest.
vocabulary.translation: 我们沿着一条蜿蜒的小径穿过森林。

vocabulary.example: They spent the weekend hiking in the mountains.
vocabulary.translation: 他们周末去山里徒步旅行了。

vocabulary.example: The car plunged over the cliff into the sea.
vocabulary.translation: 汽车冲下悬崖坠入大海。

vocabulary.example: We spent a week exploring the coastline.
vocabulary.translation: 我们花了一周时间探索海岸线。

vocabulary.entry: **pre-book** /ˌpriː ˈbʊk/ v. 预订；预先订购
vocabulary.example: It is advisable to pre-book tickets for the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 建议提前预订音乐会门票。

vocabulary.example: The prices vary depending on the season.
vocabulary.translation: 价格随季节而变化。

vocabulary.example: He only takes an occasional day off work.
vocabulary.translation: 他只是偶尔休息一天。

vocabulary.entry: **well-deserved** /ˌwel dɪˈzɜːvd/ adj. 当之无愧的；应得的
vocabulary.example: After a long week, she enjoyed a well-deserved rest.
vocabulary.translation: 漫长的一周后，她享受了应得的休息。

vocabulary.entry: **embark on** /ɪmˈbɑːk ɒn/ phr. v. 开始；着手（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He embarked on a new career as a teacher.
vocabulary.translation: 他开始了当老师的新职业生涯。

vocabulary.entry: **zigzag** /ˈzɪɡzæɡ/ v. 曲折行进；呈之字形移动
vocabulary.example: The path zigzagged up the steep hillside.
vocabulary.translation: 小路沿着陡峭的山坡蜿蜒而上。

vocabulary.example: The continent of Asia is the largest in the world.
vocabulary.translation: 亚洲大陆是世界上最大的大陆。

vocabulary.entry: **diversity** /daɪˈvɜːsəti/ n. 多样性；多样化（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There is a wide diversity of opinion on this issue.
vocabulary.translation: 关于这个问题存在广泛多样的意见。

vocabulary.entry: **shoestring budget** /ˈʃuːstrɪŋ ˈbʌdʒɪt/ n. 极少的预算（口语）
vocabulary.example: The film was made on a shoestring budget.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影是用极少的预算拍成的。

vocabulary.entry: **odd jobs** /ˌɒd ˈdʒɒbz/ n. 零工；杂活
vocabulary.example: He earned some money doing odd jobs for neighbors.
vocabulary.translation: 他靠为邻居打零工赚些钱。

vocabulary.entry: **rely on** /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ phr. v. 依赖；依靠
vocabulary.example: Many people now rely on the internet for news.
vocabulary.translation: 现在许多人依赖互联网获取新闻。

vocabulary.example: I will never forget your kindness to me.
vocabulary.translation: 我永远不会忘记你对我的好意。

vocabulary.example: He warned children not to talk to strangers.
vocabulary.translation: 他警告孩子们不要和陌生人说话。

vocabulary.example: We finally reached our destination after a long flight.
vocabulary.translation: 经过长途飞行，我们终于到达了目的地。

vocabulary.entry: **stick to** /ˈstɪk tu/ phr. v. 坚持；信守
vocabulary.example: If you stick to your goals, you will succeed eventually.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你坚持你的目标，你最终会成功的。
